subject: Post-demo follow-up: clarifying p95/p99 targets and streaming chunk behavior
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex@novusai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@novusai.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today — latency & streaming clarifications

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo — the streaming behavior looked promising. Before we move to a deeper POC, a couple of clarifications from our infra/ops side:

- Our SLOs are defined at the end-to-end request level (client -> app -> model -> response streamed back). We target p95 < 200ms and p99 < 600ms for single-turn chat responses (avg response ~80 tokens). Is the hosted API you showed able to demonstrate those across mixed traffic (50% short replies, 30% long replies, 20% streaming transcripts)?
- For streaming, we care about per-chunk emission latency (first-chunk and inter-chunk) because our UI shows incremental tokens — what are realistic p95/p99 numbers there?
- Concurrency: we expect steady-state 700 qps with bursts up to 2,200 qps for short windows. Any concerns with autoscaling / cold-starts on Hosted?

Also attaching our traffic envelope and a sample transcript to make this concrete — happy to hop on a short call with Ops/Infra if helpful.

Alex
Alex Li
Platform Engineer, NovusAI
attachments: [novus-traffic-envelope.csv]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — latency & streaming clarifications

Alex — great questions, thanks for the specifics and the envelope. Quick high-level answers, then well provide concrete numbers and a short test plan: 

- End-to-end SLOs: Our hosted API under the demo profile (model variant + 16GB KV cache, continuous batching enabled, latency-first kernel selection) has historically met p95 ~120ms and p99 ~420ms for workloads similar to what you described (80	avg tokens) in our internal synthetic streaming tests. Well validate against your exact envelope.
- Streaming chunk latencies: typical first-chunk p95 is 45-75ms (includes cold prefix/processing), inter-chunk p95 is 15-30ms; p99 inter-chunk can spike (200	-	450ms) under extreme tail circumstances depending on batching windows and KV cache hit patterns. We have mitigation knobs (smaller batching slices for streaming routes, aggressive prefix caching) to tighten that tail.
- Concurrency/scale: Hosted autoscaling is designed for your burst profile. For 700 sustained qps with 2,200 bursts, we recommend configuring a dedicated pool (reserved burst capacity) for predictable tail behavior; otherwise, cross-tenant noisy neighbors can increase p99.

Action plan (short):
1) Naomi to map our synthetic test to your envelope and run a quick shadow run (target: reproduce your mix and report p95/p99 for end-to-end and per-chunk).
2) Ben will validate the hosted autoscale configuration and recommend a dedicated pool vs. burst policy.
3) Ill coordinate a 30-min ops call for Friday to review results and agree acceptance criteria.

Deliverables: initial test report + short-run logs (we'll redact any internal tokens) and a proposed SLO wording for contract.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: [redwood-slo-proposal.pdf]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — mapping Novus envelope -> test harness

Karthik / Ben — I pulled the CSV and sketched a test mapping. Notes below (keeps technical detail for Ops):

- Traffic mix: Ill emulate 50% short (20-40 tokens), 30% medium (70-120 tokens), 20% long (200-400 tokens). Token-generation rate per request will follow the attached envelope.
- Test harness: will run two scenarios: (A) steady ramp to 700 qps for 30m (validate p95/p99) and (B) sustained 700 qps + two 10m bursts to 2,200 qps. Each scenario will capture: total e2e latency, first-chunk emission, inter-chunk latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes observed, and KV cache hit rates.
- Hypothesis: with our default batching (max batch period 12ms) and prefix caching, we should hit p95 ~120-150ms and p99 ~400-520ms for your mix in Hosted. Key risk: if client-side latency adds >50ms (network + UI rendering), your end-to-end p99 can exceed 600ms — we should measure from a representative client in the same region.

Ill spin this up today and aim to post initial numbers by EOD tomorrow (Thu). If results look close but p99 is off, we can run a second pass with: 1) lower batching windows for the streaming route, 2) quantized model variants for faster kernel paths, 3) reserved pool to reduce cross-tenant variance.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: [test-mapping-notes.txt]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — latency & streaming clarifications

Alex — quick update and next steps after Naomis mapping run (summary + concrete asks below):

Summary of early synthetic run (hosted profile, redwood-s1-small, continuous batching on):
- End-to-end (client->response finished): p95 = 138ms, p99 = 468ms (measured from our proxy in us-west-2; client-side network not included).
- Streaming: first-chunk p95 = 62ms, inter-chunk p95 = 22ms, inter-chunk p99 = 320ms. We saw a few tail spikes ~800ms tied to large batches pulled in during a burst window (batcher closed on a long request).
- Observed concurrency during the burst scenario matched the envelope; batch sizes increased under burst which drove the few p99 spikes. KV cache hit rate was ~86% in this run.

Proposed mitigations and next steps:
1) Shadow run from Novus client (owner: Ben) — run your client from us-west-2 to capture realistic client-network overhead (target date: Mon 6/7).
2) Streaming route tuning (owner: Naomi) — short-term: reduce max batch period for streaming routes to 6ms and pin streaming model variant with aggressive prefix caching. Re-run burst scenario and report delta. Deadline: Wed 6/9.
3) Capacity policy (owner: Karthik) — recommend a small reserved pool to cover 2	x of steady qps (i.e., reserve for 1,400 qps) with burst elasticity to 2,500 qps. I'll send a cost/latency tradeoff note by EOD Friday.
4) Acceptance criteria doc (owner: Karthik) — draft an SLO blurb we can use in the pilot contract: e2e p95 <= 200ms, e2e p99 <= 600ms across the agreed traffic envelope; streaming inter-chunk p95 <= 30ms, p99 <= 500ms. If we need tighter p99, we'll agree an upgrade path (dedicated pool + smaller batching).

Can we lock a 30-minute ops call for Mon 6/7 10:00am PT to walk the shadow run plan and confirm who's running it from your side? If that works, Alex please confirm and Ben / Naomi will get the runs scheduled.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
